fatal_blockers: Only Proposal 2 is worth one experiment. Proposal 1 is necessary specification work, but checking one two-stage certificate for C8 cannot discriminate the quantified U0* statement or establish asymptotic exclusion.

The actual family C_S and the semantics of finite refinement, markings, and bounded-width equality expansion are not frozen. Unless equality contraction is formally minor-preserving, an expansion may invalidate the proposed separator invariant; adding an unstated locality restriction would weaken U0 rather than prove it.

Proposal 2 has no class-side theorem: bounded recursive separator profile is especially unverified for generalized n-fold and arbitrary tree-fold instances. Its proposed MILP computes a separator of the whole graph, not the hereditary recursive profile it claims, and three finite values cannot establish Omega(S).

Proposals 3 and 4 are killed: detector incidence expansion does not by itself supply linear code branch complexity or a graphic expander matroid minor. Their puncturing, shortening, extension, branch-depth, and fixed-class closure claims are unsupported, while the identity block may destroy the intended witness.

Proposal 5 is killed because bounded twin-width for all four normal-form classes and preservation under the permitted equality interpretations are unproved. Optimizing twin-width at sizes 8 and 16 would not test either closure claim.

Proposal 6 is killed because fixed-depth tree-fold structures can use nonisomorphic subtrees or auxiliary wiring to become rigid; finite-template membership does not generally force an automorphism descending to D_S. Internal symmetries of an expansion also need not induce a nontrivial symmetry after contraction.

Proposal 7 is killed as stated: one shared template fitting finitely many sizes does not refute U0, which permits finite exceptions, and finite UNSAT has no force without a proved uniform pumping bound. The proposed q,w<=2 two-stage search covers only a narrow subclass.

All proposals address only U0. They do not pass the current unrestricted signed-kernel, affine collision, DROP, carry/lumpability, recurrence, or U1-U4 gates, so even a finite separator pass would establish no hardness or dimension-dependent gap.
evidence: ROADMAP explicitly places U0 at the frontier and names growing separator rank or marked neighborhood diversity as intended invariants. Thus Proposal 2, after correcting its measured quantity, is the only proposal directly aligned with the authorized frontier experiment.

No verifier evidence is supplied for any Fable proposal, and no serialized C8, C16, or C32 accompanies them. Their claimed closure and lower-bound mechanisms are therefore conjectures, not experimental results.

The supplied Generation-7 verifiers establish only finite quadratic-character ghosts, a synchronized COPY-cycle failure, and local Lean identities. They provide no evidence for fixed-block exclusion, separator growth, or any proposed U0 invariant.
STATUS and ROADMAP state that no hardness lemma exists and that fixed-block tractability remains mandatory. Existing finite passes and kills cannot be promoted into an asymptotic separator theorem.
next_experiment: Run exactly one hash-frozen separator-profile audit for Proposal 2. First freeze explicit C8,C16,C32, markings, and a minor-preserving definition of admissible equality contraction; then compute the exact hereditary recursive balanced-separator profile, not merely the top-level separator, with independently checked MILP certificates. Before solving, declare a constant alpha>0 from the detector design; kill the proposal unless every instance certifies profile at least alpha*S with strict growth across 8,16,32, or if any generated fixed-template example from the four claimed classes violates the proposed template-dependent bound. A pass is only finite evidence authorizing formulation of the four separate Lean closure lemmas.
